big_case_rationale: A 12-1 procedural split (judge vs. jury on trademark strength) with PepsiCo as respondent: consequential for trademark litigation practice and summary-judgment rates, but technical and low-salience for the general public.

semantic_claims.proposition: The majority will hold that trademark strength - conceptual as well as acquired - is a question of fact in the 15 U.S.C. 1114 likelihood-of-confusion analysis, resting on Hana Financial v. Hana Bank: an inquiry that turns on how ordinary consumers perceive a mark falls within the ken of the factfinder, reinforced by Booking.com's teaching that a mark's character depends on its meaning to consumers; the Court will reject the Second Circuit's judge-decided, de novo treatment of conceptual strength as mischaracterizing a consumer-perception inquiry as legal.

The majority's stated ground will be categorical rather than fact-bound: a characterization rule that trademark strength is a factual issue in every Section 1114 likelihood-of-confusion case, displacing the Second Circuit's contrary rule across the board, while expressly declining to decide whether summary judgment for PepsiCo remains proper on this record - that application is left for remand.
